summary: For symmetric and alternating groups in every sufficiently large degree, any two soluble subgroups have a conjugate with trivial intersection.
scope: The first question only: one uniform eventual cutoff. The specific threshold n ≥ 21 is not proved.

summary: An explicit subgroup of Thompson’s group F is infinite and has ordinary spread exactly one.
scope: The subgroup consists of maps with equal endpoint slopes; the spread condition holds exactly for k ≤ 1. The key generation argument specializes Gili Golan-Polak’s published theorem.

summary: Every rational linear group with finitely many abstract automorphism orbits has a normal torsion-free nilpotent subgroup of bounded finite index.
scope: No finite-generation assumption. The index is at most (2n+1)^(n²), the nilpotency class at most n−1, and there is an extension to number fields.

summary: A fixed pair generates a dense subgroup of subexponential growth in the infinite iterated natural degree-five alternating wreath product.
scope: The proof establishes the logarithmic growth limit for one compatible pair in the full inverse limit. It does not establish an additional proposed explicit growth bound.

summary: A semiabelian group of order 2,592 has an irreducible nonmonomial complex representation of degree eight.
scope: A complete counterexample, with no minimal-order claim. The complement and subgroup pair from Kida’s earlier work are prior mathematical input.

summary: A parameter-free first-order formula has exactly two values generating an infinite subgroup in the residually finite integral Heisenberg group.
scope: Disproves universal conciseness for one-variable formulae, using actual first-order syntax and realization. The separate word-conciseness question 21.105 is outside scope.
